card_says: A government corporation attached to the Department of Agriculture that builds and runs the Philippines' national irrigation systems.
source_says: NIA's own 2024 annual report says that in 2022, through Executive Order 168, NIA was transferred back to the Department of Agriculture, and that in 2024, under Executive Order 69, it was transferred back to the Office of the President. The attachment the card gives holds for 2022 to 2024 and not after that transfer; the report gives no month for either order.

company: Bukhara Regional Production State Enterprise Suvokova
card_says: Named as 'Bukhara Regional Production State Enterprise Suvokova'.
source_says: World Bank project papers of 2020 give the responsible agency as 'BUKHARA REGIONAL PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE SUVOKOVA', without the word 'State', and say institutional sector reform resulted in the establishment of 14 regional Unitary Enterprise Suvokovas, without dating that reform. A presidential decree reported on 27 November 2019 converted the state unitary water supply enterprises into limited liability companies and created the joint-stock company Uzsuvtaminot. A tender for Bukhara region water supply and sewerage works, whose tender document was issued on 17 March 2025, names JSC Bukhara Suv Taminoti as the purchaser, with Uzsuvtaminot given only as the contact and submission address.

source.title: Disclosable Restructuring Paper, Uzbekistan Bukhara and Samarkand Sewerage Project (P112719)

card_says: Ukraine's state road agency, as the body responsible for the road.
source_says: The successor body's own site says the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine was established in January 2023 and 'was formed on the foundation of Ukravtodor and Ukrinfraproekt'. Ukravtodor was the responsible body at the time of the case and has since been absorbed into that agency.

source.title: About the Agency
source.publisher: State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine

company: Projects Implementation Unit for Water Infrastructure, Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources of Uzbekistan
card_says: The unit sits under the Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources of Uzbekistan.
source_says: A report published on 14 February 2018 says the Uzbek Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources 'has been split into the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Water Resources'; it names no decree and gives no effective date, so the split is dated only to that report. World Bank reporting from 2021 names the implementing body as the Project Implementation Unit under the Ministry of Water of Uzbekistan. The ministry on the card existed when the case documents were written.

source.title: Uzbek agriculture and water resources ministry split into two

company: Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning of Kosovo (MESP)
card_says: Named as the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning of Kosovo.
source_says: Kosovo's 2021 state of the environment report calls the ministry the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure (MESPI) throughout, and mentions the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning once only, among the institutions re-established after 2000. The report gives no date for the change of name.

source.title: Report on the State of the Environment 2021

card_says: Named as rePlan Inc., as the firm that worked on the resettlement.
source_says: Trade press reported on 11 August 2015 that ERM had acquired the Toronto-based social impact and risk firm, which the report calls 'rePlan' with no legal suffix. The firm has not traded independently since that date.

source.title: ERM acquires Canadian social impact and risk specialist

card_says: The card names Manila Water as the east zone concessionaire and does not state its ownership.
source_says: Manila Water's own business profile gives Trident Water as controlling shareholder with a 52.16 per cent interest, with Philwater Holdings at 19.01 per cent and Ayala Corporation at 12.26 per cent. The profile gives no date for those holdings beyond the page itself, and gives no figure for Ayala's holding at the time of the case documents.

company: Central Planning Division, Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning
card_says: The division sits in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
source_says: The project operations manual of November 2014 places the Central Planning Division within the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, so the name on the card is the name in the project documents. The gazette of 10 November 2017 assigning ministerial responsibilities under section 53 of the Saint Vincent Constitution Order 1979 gives the post as Minister of Finance, Economic Planning, Sustainable Development and Information Technology.

source.title: Extraordinary Gazette No. 59 of 2017, assignment of ministerial responsibilities
source.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

company: Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projecto (AFAP)
card_says: Named as Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projecto (AFAP).
source_says: The World Bank project agreement of March 2021 gives the entity's address block name as 'Agência Fiduciaria de Administração de Projetos' and its signature block as 'FIDUCIARY AGENCY FOR PROJECT ADMINISTRATION', and never defines the acronym AFAP; a 2024 implementation report gives the full name as 'Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP)'. Both sources use the plural 'Projetos' rather than the card's 'Projecto'.

source.title: Project Agreement for Additional Financing Grant D778-ST
